Subject: Performance buckets — exception triage and next steps

Team —

We ran the distribution checks on the Q4/2026 review and there are ~18 people who fall into the exception bucket (ratings that sit outside the expected band for their ladder + peer cluster). HR flagged these as requiring explicit leadership triage before finalizing calibration. I attached the exception workbook (exceptions_spreadsheet_v2.xlsx) and a suggested triage matrix (triage-matrix.pdf).

High level ask: can the four of us (leadership panel) review the list and agree which exceptions are candidate for adjustment, which need manager appeals, and which should remain as-is? I propose a 45-minute session to go through the top 10 by impact, then delegate the remainder to managers with HR oversight.

Proposed times (PST):
- Thu, Feb 25 10:00–10:45
- Fri, Feb 26 14:00–14:45
- Mon, Mar 1 09:30–10:15

If you can’t make those windows, suggest alternatives and I’ll coordinate. Also calling out two constraints from People Ops: any rating changes that affect compensation must be submitted by Mar 5 for the salary cycle.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter

I’ll take Fri 2/26 14:00 if Thu conflicts. A few guardrails I want on the table so we don't end up with retroactive re-rating cascade:
- We should limit calibration adjustments to explicit evidence of mis-rating (documentation mismatch, missed upward calibration due to manager error) rather than adjusting for distribution targets alone.
- Any change that would move someone >1 rating tier should require a short note from the manager + one independent reviewer.
- If the exception is driven by benchmarking vs. peers in different functions, we need to ensure ladder parity before changing bands (I can work with CompOps on quick checks).

I'll review the triage matrix and add inline comments.

Markus
VP, Engineering
